conviction_note: Mild up lean (p_up 54) on a 10-point absolute move: a consistent guide-beater going in after a 15% de-rating and sell-side target cuts, with a tariff regime that came in below the company's guide assumption and a likely IEEPA refund recognition, set against soft Europe/alt-data reads and a history of selling beat-and-raises (Q2 2026 -2.2%, Q3 2025 -12.6% on the guide). Findings sum to +1.0 and the scaled number is +0.8; they agree in sign and size, and both are small against a 9.5% implied move because the decisive line, the Q4 implied guide, is not knowable from outside.
bar: Q3 FY26 (quarter ended 2026-08-30) company guide: revenue +4-5% reported and organic (~$1.60-1.62bn on Q3 2025's $1.54bn), gross margin ~61.8%, adjusted diluted EPS $0.34-0.36 (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/levi-strauss-hebt-2026-ziele-und-kundigt-dividende-an-q2-ubertrifft-q3-eps-3436c ; revenue range in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000094845/000009484526000038/exhibit991-2q2026pressrele.htm). Consensus sits at the TOP of the guide: EPS $0.36 from 15 analysts (AAII/Zacks, 2026-10-06, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/511490-what-you-need-to-know-about-levi-strauss--cos-q3-earnings), revenue $1.61-1.62bn (earningswhispers/benzinga via search; UBS also $0.36, https://parameter.io/levi-strauss-levi-stock-wall-street-lowers-expectations-before-quarterly-report/). FY26 guide: revenue +7-7.5% (~$6.72-6.75bn), adj EPS $1.46-1.52; H1 adj EPS was $0.42 + $0.28 = $0.70, so the guide implies H2 $0.76-0.82 and Q4 ~$0.40-0.48. Bar is sourced to a company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources, so not capped.
positioning_check: Short interest 8.05m shares, 2.11% of float (MarketBeat basis, likely all share classes; Class A float basis materially higher, a snippet put it near 7%), 3.8 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-15, up 13.7% from 7.08m (1.9%, 3.45 days) on 2026-08-31 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/LEVI/short-interest). Not a crowded short. Skew 25d is -1.02 vol points (calls marginally richer than puts) with put/call OI 1.13: options balanced, no directional statement. Event-implied move 9.5% (straddle 9.87%) vs a 7-print median absolute reaction of 8.0%, max 12.55%. Tape: -2.95% over 20d, -22.6% from 52w high, and -15.3% from the 2026-07-08 print to 2026-10-06 while SPY rose 4.6% (AAII). Sell-side cut targets into the print (Citi to Neutral PT $25->$22 on 09-30, Jefferies $27->$25 on 10-01, Stifel $28->$27); consensus still Moderate Buy, avg PT ~$27.

findings.finding: Levi has beaten its own quarterly guide and consensus every print this year (Q1 FY26 adj EPS $0.42 vs ~$0.37 consensus, revenue ~$1.70bn vs $1.65bn; Q2 FY26 $0.28 vs $0.24, revenue $1.56bn vs $1.52bn, +2.8%), and the Q3 bar ($0.36 / ~$1.615bn) sits at the top of the company's $0.34-0.36 / +4-5% guide, so a repeat of the habitual 2-3% revenue beat clears it; but it lands inside the guided range and this name has sold beat-and-raises (Q2 -2.17%, Q3 2025 -12.55%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 beat ($0.28 vs $0.24) with FY raise: -2.17% close-to-close (baseline). Q1 FY26 beat and raise: +10.65%. Q3 FY25 beat with soft holiday guide: -12.55%. Beats alone have not determined the sign; the guide has.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is pinned at the guide top ($0.36), not above it, despite two consecutive ~$0.04-0.05 beats; if the market expected the habitual beat the whisper/consensus would sit above the range, and the stock would not have de-rated 15% vs SPY since July.
findings.independence: Q1 beat magnitude from a separate document: https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2897730/levi-strauss-q1-earnings-beat-estimates-dtc-revenues-up-16-yy (2026-04-07). Shares the bar with finding 4.

findings.finding: Since 2026-07-24 the US replaced the temporary Section 122 surcharge with Section 301 duties of 10% (Bangladesh, Pakistan, Cambodia, Indonesia, Mexico, Guatemala, EU and others) and 12.5% (China, Vietnam, India), while Levi's July 8 guide assumed 30% on China and 20% on Rest-of-World; on Levi's sourcing mix the realised regime sits below the guide's assumption, a gross-margin tailwind that would surface in the Q4/FY guide rather than in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY25 (2025-10-09) fell -12.55% on a guide that flagged tariff margin pressure; Q2 FY26 raised FY gross margin to +10bp and still fell -2.17%. Tariff-driven guide changes have been the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: If priced, previews would expect a gross-margin or EPS raise; instead Jefferies expects revenue guidance held and only a 'potential' EPS nudge, and targets were cut. Caveat: sources disagree on whether the prior Section 122 rate was 10% or 15% (raised to 15% on 2026-02-22 per Global Trade Alert), so the change vs the regime at guidance time is either -2.5 to -5 points or roughly flat; either way the realised rate is below Levi's stated 20% RoW assumption. Company has not confirmed the transmission, and goods sold in Q4 were partly landed before 07-24.
findings.independence: Second source for the 10%/12.5% tiers (dated 2026-07-05): https://krazykreators.com/blogs/apparel-tariffs-july-2026-forced-labor-301-regime ; Section 122 at 15%: https://globaltradealert.org/reports/S122-US-Tariff-Estimates . Levi's assumption from its own release (finding 1 source).

findings.finding: Levi paid ~$80m of IEEPA tariffs, recognised a refund asset only for CAPE phase 1 as of 2026-05-31 and said it would recognise further refunds when ASC 450 is met; CBP opened CAPE phase 2 on 2026-06-29, inside Levi's Q3 (Jun-Aug 30), and AEO booked a $179m gross-profit benefit from refunds in its quarter ended 2026-08-01, so Levi likely recognises a further refund of up to several tens of millions (roughly $0.05-0.12/share pre-adjustment) in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior Levi print carried a refund. Across the repo's resolved days refund names split by the direction of guidance; AEO beat on refunds (2026-09-09). If Levi books it in COGS and leaves it in adjusted EPS the headline beat is lower quality; if excluded it is a GAAP-only item.
findings.why_not_priced: The refund is not in the Q3 guide (the Q2 release never mentions it) and the consensus at $0.36 shows no refund uplift; if analysts had included it, Q3 EPS estimates would sit above the guided top. Sized at a fraction of the dollars because there is no stated path to the guide.

findings.finding: Expectations were reset into the print: the stock fell 15.3% from the 2026-07-08 release to 2026-10-06 while SPY rose 4.6%, and in the final week Citi moved to Neutral with PT $25->$22 (09-30), Jefferies cut $27->$25 (10-01) and Stifel $28->$27, leaving the stock at ~12.5x FY26 EPS with consensus EPS at the guide top rather than above it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 came after a drawdown and rose +10.65%; Q3 FY25 came after a rally (+11.25% on Q2 FY25) and fell -12.55%. The two largest moves in the history line up with the run-in direction reversing.
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating is itself the price; what is not priced is the asymmetry it creates for an in-line-or-better quarter. If the market were positioned for upside, skew would be call-rich and short interest falling; skew is flat (-1.02) and short interest rose 13.7% into mid-September.
findings.independence: Target cuts: https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/LEVI/forecast/ (Citi 09-30, Jefferies 10-01) and https://parameter.io/levi-strauss-levi-stock-wall-street-lowers-expectations-before-quarterly-report/ (2026-10-01). Shares the consensus bar with finding 1.

findings.finding: Europe (~27% of revenue; organic -1% in Q2 FY26) faced a soft, promotional June-August: H&M's Western Europe sales fell 1% in its Jun-Aug quarter on 'consumer caution and high levels of discounting, particularly in Germany and the UK', and Jefferies cites European marketplace challenges into this print; against that, Levi said in July that Europe DTC accelerated to +7% and guided mid-single-digit H2 growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Europe has not been the stated cause of a large Levi reaction in the history; the US wholesale/holiday guide has. Q2 FY26 Europe organic -1% sat inside a -2.17% reaction to a beat-and-raise.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-25 (H&M Q3 FY26 report covering Jun-Aug 2026; page carries no visible date, content dated by the Q3 2026 and September 2026 references)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Jefferies named it in its preview. What is not visible is a cut to Levi's Europe estimate; if it were in, consensus revenue would sit below the guide midpoint, not at its top. Proxy from a peer, net of Levi's own +7% Europe DTC statement, so sized small.
findings.independence: Jefferies preview (2026-10-01): https://blockonomi.com/levi-strauss-levi-stock-wall-street-analysts-lower-targets-before-earnings-report/ ; Levi's own Europe DTC +7% comment: https://stocktaper.com/earningsCallSummary/LEVI/2026/Q2

findings.finding: Two sell-side previews cite weak alternative data on Levi's US sales: Stifel says retail partner feedback is encouraging but alternative sales data shows weakness, and Jefferies flags 'inconsistent patterns' in US sales tracking and weakness among value-conscious shoppers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY25 fell -12.55% on a guide that pointed to weak wholesale demand; Q2 FY26 fell -2.17% while the release itself flagged a slowdown in the Signature (value) brand.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is in the wire copy and drove the target cuts. It survives as a small negative because consensus revenue still sits at the guide top rather than being cut, which is what full pricing of weak card data would look like. Secondary report of data I could not see.
findings.independence: Same note reported at https://parameter.io/levi-strauss-levi-stock-wall-street-lowers-expectations-before-quarterly-report/ (same underlying notes, not independent). Shares a document with finding 5.

findings.finding: US wholesale partners that reported for the July quarter raised their outlooks: Macy's comps +2.7% with FY guide raised and inventories 'well-positioned' (2026-09-10), Kohl's comps -0.9% but FY outlook raised (2026-08-26); denim peers were mixed: Gap comps -1% with denim strong in H1 and newer fits working, AEO brand comps -1% with older denim fits needing clearance (2026-09-09), Kontoor's Wrangler US +1% (2026-08).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wholesale was Levi's weak line in Q2 FY26 (+3% organic) and the stated reason the Q3 guide decelerated; the guide reaction (-2.17%) followed.
findings.why_not_priced: Each partner print is public, but none names Levi; healthy partner inventories and raised guides argue against a wholesale-order cut in Levi's Q4 guide, which is what the Q3 FY25 reaction punished. Proxy, sized small.

findings.finding: CFO Harmit Singh (retirement announced April 2026) leaves the CFO seat on 2026-11-01; Levi named John Vandemore (ex-Skechers CFO) on 2026-09-30, so tonight is Singh's last guide, which may be framed conservatively for the incoming CFO.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO transition in the 7-print history.
findings.why_not_priced: The appointment is public; the effect on how the Q4 guide is framed is inference only. Sized near zero.

findings.finding: Levi disclosed a cybersecurity incident on 2026-08-07 (8-K item 8.01): corporate files exfiltrated via social engineering of three employees, no consumer data affected, no operational interruption, and the company does not believe it had or is reasonably likely to have a material impact.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior incident in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two months and declared immaterial; only residual risk is a one-off cost line in the quarter.

findings.finding: FX was roughly neutral in Levi's Q3: EUR/USD traded ~1.15-1.17 through August 2026 (low of the year 1.1356 on 06-24), close to the year-ago quarter, consistent with the guide's 'no anticipated benefit from foreign exchange'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FX has not been the stated driver of a Levi reaction in the history.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price: it confirms the guide's FX assumption, which removes a source of upside or downside rather than adding one.

outside_window.finding: Kontoor's Lee divestiture closes in Q4 2026 with proceeds into a $400m ASR, a competitive-landscape change in US mass denim that would show in Levi's FY27 wholesale, not in this print.

baseline_tension: Skew is flat (-1.02) and the run-up is negative (-2.95% 20d, -15% vs the July print), so a mild up lean cuts against nothing in the options and with the drawdown; it does cut against this name's habit of selling beat-and-raises, which is why p_up is held at 54.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 and 6 (beat lands inside the guide, name sells beats): reported-quarter beat finding cut +0.5 -> +0.3
Rule 5 (macro-to-company transmission unconfirmed by the company): tariff-regime guidance finding cut +0.8 -> +0.6
Rule 5 (unexplained drawdown worth 0) checked: the de-rating here is explained by dated target cuts, so kept, but trimmed +0.8 -> +0.6 as positioning inference
Rules 5 and 9 (peer proxy vs the company's own Europe DTC +7% statement; segment net of rest): Europe finding cut -0.8 -> -0.5
Rule 3 (own caveat: Stifel also says retailer feedback is encouraging): alt-data finding cut -0.5 -> -0.3
CFO transition trimmed -0.2 -> -0.1 as pure inference
Rule 2 (one-off refund with no path to the guide): left at +0.3, already sized as a fraction of the dollars
Rule 8 / core (understatement): abs_move_pct raised 9.5 -> 10.0 for a guidance-heavy print with a CFO handover; p_up left at 54
Net: per-finding sizes moved but the sum is unchanged at +1.0 by coincidence of offsetting cuts
